title: Microsoft Dataverse: Python SDK for scripting and agent workflows
summary: The briefing's roadmap facts, licensing statements and governance calls are supported. The application-user UI path is accurate but stops before the security-role selector; extending it would make the control easier to follow.

claims.quote: "status": "Launched"

claims.claim: The roadmap lists General Availability as a release phase.

claims.claim: The roadmap also lists Preview as a release phase.

claims.claim: The SDK lets Python developers access and manipulate Dataverse data without .NET knowledge.
claims.quote: You can easily access, manage, and manipulate data stored in Dataverse by using familiar Python syntax. You don't need any .NET knowledge.

claims.quote: The SDK for Python is published under open-source licensing.

claims.claim: The overview documents create, retrieve, update and delete operations.
claims.quote: Support for create, retrieve, update, and delete data operations by using a single request.

claims.claim: Bulk operations use CreateMultiple.
claims.quote: This feature uses Dataverse's native CreateMultiple, UpdateMultiple, UpsertMultiple, and BulkDelete Web API operations

claims.claim: Bulk operations use UpdateMultiple.
claims.quote: This feature uses Dataverse's native CreateMultiple, UpdateMultiple, UpsertMultiple, and BulkDelete Web API operations

claims.claim: Bulk operations can remove multiple rows using BulkDelete.
claims.quote: Specify multiple operations in a single web service call. This feature uses Dataverse's native CreateMultiple, UpdateMultiple, UpsertMultiple, and BulkDelete Web API operations

claims.claim: The overview documents read-only direct SQL SELECT queries.
claims.quote: Supports simple read-only "SELECT" statements with paging.

claims.claim: The SDK provides pandas DataFrame wrappers.
claims.quote: Client wrappers are provided for all CRUD operations where DataFrames and Series data types are returned to the caller.

claims.claim: The SDK uploads files to file columns.
claims.quote: Upload files to a Dataverse file column with automatic chunking for large files.

claims.claim: The SDK supports batch requests.
claims.quote: Send multiple CRUD, table metadata, and SQL query operations in a single HTTP request with optional transactional changesets.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The SDK supports creating, updating and deleting custom columns.
claims.quote: The SDK supports create, update, and delete (CUD) of custom tables and columns

claims.claim: The SDK provides structured error handling.
claims.quote: Error handling: structured exception hierarchy with detailed error context and retry guidance.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: HTTP diagnostics logging is opt-in and writes all HTTP requests and responses to a file.
claims.quote: HTTP diagnostics logging: opt-in file-based logging of all HTTP requests and responses

claims.claim: HTTP diagnostics logging redacts sensitive headers such as authorization.
claims.quote: with automatic redaction of sensitive headers, such as authorization.

claims.claim: The SDK internally calls the Dataverse Web API.
claims.quote: The SDK provides a Python programming interface that internally calls the Dataverse Web API.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope
claims.claim: Authentication and application identity use the Azure Identity credential supplied to the client.
claims.quote: The SDK client requires any Azure Identity TokenCredential implementation for OAuth authentication with Dataverse.

claims.claim: The roadmap names autonomous data agents as a capability it can include.
claims.quote:
Key capabilities can include:

- Autonomous data agents that can query, update, and evaluate data quality

claims.claim: The roadmap names form prediction and autofill as potential capabilities.
claims.quote: - Form prediction and autofill

claims.claim: The roadmap names potential Model Context Protocol support.
claims.quote: - Support for agentic primitives like Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Agent-to-Agent (A2A) collaboration

claims.claim: The roadmap names potential Agent-to-Agent collaboration.

claims.quote: Searched: autonomous data agents, form prediction, autofill, MCP and A2A in the opened SDK overview; its complete feature list names none.

claims.claim: The roadmap says enabled for admins/makers/marketers automatically.
claims.quote: Enabled for admins/makers/marketers automatically

claims.claim: Learn documents installing the package with pip install PowerPlatform-Dataverse-Client.
claims.quote: pip install PowerPlatform-Dataverse-Client

claims.claim: Getting started requires Python 3.10+.
claims.quote: An activated Python 3.10+ environment.

claims.claim: The reference architecture instead requires Python 3.13 or later.
claims.quote: Python 3.13 or later

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; What's changing; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The SDK is user-opt-in: developers choose to install and use the package.
claims.quote: From a terminal window, run the following command. This command installs the latest stable release of the SDK from a pypi.org package.

claims.claim: The SDK accesses existing Dataverse data rather than adding a new data store.
claims.quote: You can easily access, manage, and manipulate data stored in Dataverse by using familiar Python syntax.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Scope; rationale: risk
claims.claim: SDK data operations enforce existing Dataverse security roles rather than a separate permission model.
claims.quote: Role-based access control: Enforces Dataverse security roles and policies for all data operations.

claims.where: controls[3].ui and .api; summary; Why it matters; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no tenant or environment switch specific to allowing or blocking the Python SDK.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse SDK Python admin setting tenant environment disable switch; opened overview, get-started, quick-guide-dataverse, app access control and pac env. Results describe installation, roles and general app controls, not an SDK-specific UI or API switch.

claims.claim: The SDK can extract Dataverse tables into pandas DataFrames.
claims.quote: Extract and transform: Load tables into Pandas DataFrames for cleaning, feature engineering, and exploratory analysis.

claims.claim: Extracted data is no longer protected by the Dataverse security boundary.
claims.quote: after the data has been extracted it is no longer protected by the security boundary provided by Dynamics 365 (online) and is instead controlled directly by the customer.

claims.claim: Getting started shows InteractiveBrowserCredential and AzureCliCredential as development options.
claims.quote:
# Development options
credential = InteractiveBrowserCredential()  # Browser authentication
# credential = AzureCliCredential()

claims.claim: Getting started shows ClientSecretCredential and CertificateCredential as production options.
claims.quote:
# Production options
# credential = ClientSecretCredential(tenant_id, client_id, client_secret)
# credential = CertificateCredential(tenant_id, client_id, cert_path)

claims.claim: Application users give registered applications access to an environment.
claims.quote: You can create an unlicensed application user in your environment. This application user is given access to your environment's data on behalf of the user who's using your application.

claims.where: controls[0]; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Why it matters
claims.claim: App access control allows or blocks client app IDs at the Dataverse authentication layer.
claims.quote: Dataverse authentication validates the client app ID in the user’s token against a list of allowed and blocked apps configured for the environment.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: App access control requires a managed environment.
claims.quote: Your environment must be a managed environment.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: App access control does not cover partner service-to-service calls; Microsoft points to deactivating or deleting their application users.
claims.quote:
Partner apps with service-to-service calls

To block these apps, make them inactive or delete them from the environment in the Power Platform admin center.

claims.claim: InteractiveBrowserCredential accepts a client_id.
claims.quote: client_id ... Client ID of the Microsoft Entra application that users will sign into.

claims.claim: Without client_id, InteractiveBrowserCredential uses an Azure development application.
claims.quote: If not specified, users will authenticate to an Azure development application, which is not recommended for production scenarios.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance
claims.claim: client.files.upload automatically creates a missing file column.
claims.quote: If the file column doesn't exist, the SDK creates it automatically.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Automatic creation of a file column is a permanent schema change.
claims.quote: the new column becomes a permanent part of your environment's schema.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Microsoft advises creating file columns in advance in production.
claims.quote: In production environments, create file columns in advance rather than relying on automatic creation.

claims.claim: Running dataverse-install-claude-skill after package installation optionally installs two Claude skills.
claims.quote:
you can optionally install two Claude Skills when installing the SDK from a package.

pip install PowerPlatform-Dataverse-Client && dataverse-install-claude-skill

claims.claim: The installed Claude skill definitions are stored on the development computer.
claims.quote: you can find skill definitions in the `.claude/skills/dataverse-sdk-use/SKILL.md` and `.claude/skills/dataverse-sdk-dev/SKILL.md` files on your development computer.

claims.claim: The SDK retries operations affected by throttling.
claims.quote: Automatic retries ... operations that fail due to temporary problems, such as API throttling or service unavailability.

claims.claim: Dataverse service protection limits apply to external web service requests.
claims.quote: Service protection limits apply to all external web service requests, not only the CRUD operations on tables counted against entitlement limits.

claims.claim: Heavy scripts can affect other callers sharing the same user account.
claims.quote: We limit the number of concurrent connections per user account, the number of API requests per connection, and the amount of execution time that can be used for each connection.

claims.claim: Getting-started prerequisites list environment read/write access, OAuth, Python and PyPI access but no Microsoft licence.
claims.quote: Read/write access to a Dataverse environment. ... OAuth authentication configured for your application. ... An activated Python 3.10+ environment. ... Pandas version 2.0.0+. ... Network access to https://pypi.org

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft has not published an SDK-specific Microsoft licence requirement.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse SDK for Python pricing license and licensing entitlement. Opened overview, get-started, OAuth authentication and table licensing; they document open-source licensing and Dataverse entitlements, not an SDK-specific Microsoft licence.

claims.claim: Using an ordinary user's credentials for an unattended app requires a paid licence for that account.
claims.quote: While you could achieve these scenarios by using credentials for an ordinary user, that user account needs a paid license. Don't use this approach.

claims.claim: An application user bound to a registered Microsoft Entra app does not consume a paid licence.
claims.quote: create a special application user that is bound to a Microsoft Entra ID registered application. ... Another benefit of this approach is that it doesn't consume a paid license.

claims.claim: Users can create custom tables with a Dynamics 365, Power Apps or Power Automate licence.
claims.quote: Users can create custom tables with Dynamics 365, Power Apps, or Power Automate license

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The licensing model is included under existing Dataverse entitlements rather than a new SDK add-on.
claims.quote: Users can create custom tables with Dynamics 365, Power Apps, or Power Automate license

claims.claim: Dataverse CRUD, assign and share operations from SDK traffic count toward request limits like other clients using SOAP or REST.
claims.quote: All create, read, update, and delete (CRUD), assign, and share operations ... These operations can be from any client or application (including Dynamics 365) and use any endpoint (SOAP or REST).

claims.claim: Application, non-interactive, administrative and system users share tenant-level request limits.
claims.quote: These limits are defined and pooled at the tenant level. ... Application users ... Non-interactive users ... Administrative users ... SYSTEM user

claims.claim: No SDK-specific meter or charge is documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse SDK Python pricing meter charge license; opened SDK overview, get-started, request limits and capacity-storage. These name open-source licensing, general request entitlements and storage capacity, not an SDK-specific meter.

claims.claim: Scripts that write rows or files can increase Dataverse storage consumption.
claims.quote: All Dataverse tables, including system tables, are included in the storage capacity reports. Files such as .pdf (or any other file attachment type) are stored in file storage.

claims.claim: Schema changes require appropriate customization privileges.
claims.quote: Creating a column is a metadata change: you need privileges to customize the table

claims.claim: Learn documents installing from PyPI or the GitHub source repository.
claims.quote: Run the following command to install the SDK from the project's GitHub source instead of from the package. Install the client from the PyPi package or from the source, but not both.

claims.claim: App access control is at Security > Identity and access > App access control > environment > Set up app access control > Access control.
claims.quote: select Security. ... select Identity and access. ... select App access control ... Select the environment ... Select the Set up app access control button. ... Access control dropdown list.

claims.claim: pac env update-settings --environment <environment-url> --name applicationbasedaccesscontrolmode --value <mode> changes the environment's app-control mode, not its individual app lists.
claims.quote: pac env update-settings ... --name ... Name of the setting to update ... --environment ... Guid or absolute https URL. ... --value ... Value to which setting should be updated to

claims.claim: App access control prerequisites name the Power Platform admin or Dynamics 365 admin role.
claims.quote: Verify your role ... Power Platform admin ... Dynamics 365 admin

claims.claim: Application users and their roles are configured through Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Application users > + New app user > + Add an app.
claims.quote: Select + New app user ... Select + Add an app ... Under Business Unit, select a business unit ... Select the edit icon to select security roles for the new application user.
claims.fix: Extend controls[1].ui.path to 'Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Application users > + New app user > + Add an app > security roles edit icon'. Keep the note instructing readers to choose the app and business unit. The cited application-users page documents the remaining selector.

claims.claim: POST https://api.bap.microsoft.com/providers/Microsoft.BusinessAppPlatform/scopes/admin/environments/{environmentIdGuid}/addAppUser?api-version=2020-10-01 creates an application user.
claims.quote: POST https://api.bap.microsoft.com/providers/Microsoft.BusinessAppPlatform/scopes/admin/environments/{environmentIdGuid}/addAppUser?api-version=2020-10-01

claims.claim: The application-user creation API page is preview documentation.
claims.quote:
Create a Dataverse application user (preview)

[This article is pre-release documentation and is subject to change.]

claims.claim: The application-user creation API always assigns System Administrator.
claims.quote: This always adds the application user as a System Administrator.

claims.claim: The application-user creation request body sets servicePrincipalAppId to the registered app's client ID.
claims.quote: "servicePrincipalAppId": "AzureAD_App_Registration_ClientID"

claims.claim: The application-user UI lets the admin choose the business unit and select security roles using the edit icon.
claims.quote: Under Business Unit, select a business unit from the dropdown list. ... Select the edit icon to select security roles for the new application user.

claims.claim: Environment auditing is at Security > Compliance > Auditing > environment > Set up auditing > Turn on auditing.
claims.quote: select Security > Compliance. ... Select the Auditing tile. ... Select the environment ... Select Set up auditing. In the Auditing pane, select Turn on auditing.

claims.claim: PATCH [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/organizations([Organization ID]) updates organization auditing settings.
claims.quote: Change the column values in the organization table to change how auditing works for the environment. ... PATCH [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/organizations([Organization ID]) HTTP/1.1

claims.claim: Changing auditing configuration requires System Administrator or System Customizer.
claims.quote: you must have the System Administrator or System Customizer role to change the settings.

claims.claim: The PATCH body uses isauditenabled for environment auditing and isuseraccessauditenabled for user-access logging.
claims.quote: isauditenabled ... Whether auditing is enabled for the environment ... isuseraccessauditenabled ... Whether user access logging is enabled

claims.claim: Recording data changes requires environment, table and column auditing.
claims.quote: First, turn on auditing at the environment level. To log data changes in a table, turn on auditing for the table and for the column.

claims.claim: User-access logging requires Log access in addition to environment auditing.
claims.quote: To turn on user access auditing (log access) or activity logging (Read logs), turn on auditing at the environment level. ... Log access | Log whenever the system is accessed, generally by signing in.

claims.claim: ApplicationBasedAccessDenied is an audit event administrators can review for app access control.
claims.quote: Select the dropdown arrow near the Event heading, then find and select ApplicationBasedAccessDenied and ApplicationBasedAccessAllowed.

claims.claim: ApplicationBasedAccessAllowed is an audit event administrators can review for app access control.
claims.quote: Select the dropdown arrow near the Event heading, then find and select ApplicationBasedAccessDenied and ApplicationBasedAccessAllowed.

claims.claim: The organization table's applicationbasedaccesscontrolmode column stores the app access control mode.
claims.quote: ApplicationBasedAccessControlMode ... DisplayName | Application Based Access Control Mode ... LogicalName | applicationbasedaccesscontrolmode

claims.claim: Security roles for users are assigned under the environment's Users + permissions settings.
claims.quote: Select Users + permissions > Security roles. ... Select Members ... select the + Add people.
